cases.note: The loop checks the same thresholds (map.pb through map.kb) in the same largest-to-smallest order as the original else-if chain, breaking on the first match and defaulting to 'B' otherwise, so the selected unit is identical for every input. The var declarations hoist without conflict, making this a purely equivalent refactor.

The diff replaces [-+]? with [^-+]? in the core int tag's explicit-tag pattern, so explicitly tagged signed binary integers no longer match: load('!!int "-0b1010"') now throws a YAMLException instead of returning -10. The sibling int_json/int_yaml11 patterns and parseYamlInteger$2's sign handling show signed binary was meant to be supported.

cases.note: The refactor only hoists the digits.slice(2) computation into a 'rest' constant before the prefix checks; 'rest' is still only used in the 0b/0o/0x branches where it equals the previously computed value.slice(2), and the decimal branch is untouched. Since String.prototype.slice is side-effect free, load/dump behaviour for all integer forms (e.g. 0x1F, 0o17, -0b101, decimal) is identical.

Replacing `type === 'string'` with `true` makes `val.length` evaluate for every input: ms(null)/ms(undefined) now throw a TypeError instead of the documented Error, and non-string values with a non-zero length (e.g. ms(['2 days'])) are silently parsed into a number instead of throwing. Ordinary string and number inputs are unaffected, so the existing suite stays green.

Formatting never emits years in 2.1.3, so only year parsing is observably broken.
